title: Haah's 3D cubic code thermalizes rapidly
authors: Sebastian Stengele, Libor Caha, Ángela Capel, Simone Warzel
abstract: Haah's 3D cubic code was introduced as a candidate for a self-correcting quantum memory in three dimensions, using the absence of string logical operators to obstruct thermal errors. It has been a long-standing open question whether it is a self-correcting quantum memory. Even though the memory time was explored numerically, no analytical upper bound was known. Here, we settle this question rigorously and show that the cubic code thermalizes rapidly at every positive temperature. Our proof relies on the framework of [Commun. Math. Phys. 407, 195 (2026)] to turn a decay-of-correlations condition into a modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality for the Davies generator. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first analytic proof of rapid mixing for all positive temperatures for any fracton code.
summary: The authors prove that Haah's 3D cubic code rapidly thermalizes at any positive temperature, settling a long-standing open question in quantum memory research. They achieve this by establishing a modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality for the system's dynamics. This result provides a rigorous, analytically derived bound on the memory time, confirming its robustness against thermal noise.
main_problem: The paper rigorously determines whether Haah's 3D cubic code, a candidate for a self-correcting quantum memory, thermalizes rapidly at any positive temperature.
main_result: It proves that the cubic code's dynamics mix rapidly at all positive temperatures, establishing an upper bound on the passive-memory time that grows only logarithmically with system size.
method: The proof adapts techniques from classical spin systems, utilizing the framework of modified logarithmic Sobolev inequalities (MLSI) derived from the decay-of-correlations condition (Dobrushin-Shlosman condition).
model_or_system: The system is Haah's 3D cubic code, defined on a discrete torus, whose thermal dynamics are governed by a Lindbladian generator derived from local X and Z bath couplings.
key_observables: Mixing time ($t_{	ext{mix}}(\epsilon)$), Modified Logarithmic Sobolev Inequality (MLSI) constant ($\alpha$), and the decay of boundary correlation quantities ($	ext{DS}_{\#}$).
important_parameters: Positive inverse temperature ($ eta < \infty$), system size ($L_{\Lambda}$), and the error tolerance ($\epsilon$).
main_assumptions: The initial analysis assumes periodic boundary conditions, though the result is expected to extend to open boundary conditions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the geometry used in the multiscale analysis, showing partitions of boxes ($\Sigma_B$) and the geometric setup for both periodic and open boundary conditions.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the general framework using the MLSI derived from the DS-condition, then developing a multiscale analysis to prove the DS-condition itself, and finally using this bound to prove the rapid mixing of the dynamics.
why_interesting: This work provides a major theoretical breakthrough by analytically proving rapid mixing for a key quantum error-correcting code, moving beyond previous reliance on energy barriers.
